answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a stake that decays slowly over time, like a vine that must keep growing to stay alive. New identities start in a meadow of untrusted newcomers where they earn reputation only by completing verified work and attesting others honest transactions. If an agent defects, its stake burns like an ember going cold, forfeited and distributed to honest peers, so creating thousands of cheap identities costs far more than any fraud could return.
